title: Ground Safety Specialist (MSgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC CD&I
raw_text:
4.     MOS 8012, Ground Safety Specialist (MSgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC CD&I

    a. Summary. A trained Marine able to manage or assist in the operation
of the Marine Corps Ground Safety Program in compliance with the Code of
Federal Regulations.

       b.   Prerequisites.   None.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete one of the HQMC (SD) approved Ground Safety Courses:

                (a) M02M8SS, MCB Quantico, VA.

                (b) M26M8SS, MCAS Iwakuma, Japan.

                (c) M21M8S3, MCB Kaneohe Bay, HI.

                (d) M03M8SS, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC.

                (e) M10M8SA, MCB Camp Pendleton, CA.

                (f) M44M8S2 or MARFORRES, New Orleans, LA.

                (g) M22M8S3, MCB Camp Butler, Okinawa, Japan.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Assists in planning and directing the Accident Prevention Program
of the command.

            (2) Maintains safety directives and accident reports.

            (3) Investigates accidents and conducts periodic safety inspections.

        (4) Provides safety indoctrination and education for the command and
obtains and maintains safety equipment and material.




                                         3-460                       Enclosure (1)
 3149                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



        (5) Advises and assists in the organization and implementation of a
complete vehicle safety program for both Government and private motor vehicle
operation.

        (6) Monitors compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health
Administration (OSHA) requirements.

            (7) Conducts Operational Risk Management (ORM) assessments.

            (8) Applies hazard control fundamentals and techniques.

            (9) Facilitates the Industrial Hygiene Program.

        (10) Supervises the Hazardous Materials, Waste, and Pollution
Prevention Programs.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Occupational Health and Safety Specialists 29-9011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

d. Duties (1) Assists in planning and directing the Accident Prevention Program of the command.
Complete accident reports when necessary.
(2) Maintains safety directives and accident reports.
Investigate and report on accidents.
(3) Investigates accidents and conducts periodic safety inspections.
Conduct safety training or education programs and demonstrate the use of safety equipment.
(4) Provides safety indoctrination and education for the command and obtains and maintains safety equipment and material.
Provide for public safety by maintaining order, responding to emergencies, protecting people and property, enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws, and promoting good community relations.
(5) Advises and assists in the organization and implementation of a complete vehicle safety program for both Government and private motor vehicle operation.
Monitor operations to ensure compliance with applicable health, safety, or hygiene standards.
(6) Monitors compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requirements.
Prepare operational or risk reports for management analysis.
(7) Conducts Operational Risk Management (ORM) assessments.
Recommend procedures for detection, prevention, and elimination of physical, chemical, or other product hazards.
(8) Applies hazard control fundamentals and techniques.
Plan and conduct industrial hygiene research.
(9) Facilitates the Industrial Hygiene Program.
Participate in the development of spill prevention programs and hazardous waste rules and regulations, and recommend corrective actions for hazardous waste problems.
(10) Supervises the Hazardous Materials, Waste, and Pollution Prevention Programs.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
